title: YRDSB reviews rules for school boundaries, student transfers, and overflow
executiveSummary: Trustees will review updated YRDSB rules governing school boundaries, student transfers, holding schools, and French Immersion programs.
The board recommends sending the updated boundary and student transfer policy out for six months of public feedback.
Trustees will vote on revising the board's operational bylaws to align with new provincial education legislation.
studentParentImpact: The updated YRDSB policy clarifies how school boundaries are set, how primary French Immersion dual track programs are introduced, and how students directed to overflow or holding schools get recalled to their home schools. It also details the rules and limits for student transfer requests. Families can share feedback on these changes during a six-month public consultation period by submitting comments online or through their local school council, or by emailing policy.committee@yrdsb.ca.
policyChanges: YRDSB is updating Policy #108.0 on student accommodation and transfers, Policy #422.0 on facility partnerships, and Policy #445.0 on school naming. Trustees will also vote on revising the board's Operational By-Law to comply with provincial legislation.

title: YRDSB Trustees Review Child Protection Policy and Launch Family Support Office
executiveSummary: Trustees will consider final approval for YRDSB Policy 610.0 on reporting children and youth in need of protection.
YRDSB has launched a new Student and Family Support Office to help parents resolve school issues.
Fall early reading screening for primary students across York Region will begin in late September.
studentParentImpact: York Region District School Board families have a new avenue to address concerns through the recently launched Student and Family Support Office. If parents cannot resolve an issue with their child's teacher or principal, they can contact this office via phone, email, or an online form. Parents of students in Kindergarten Year 2, Grade 1, and Grade 2 should also expect early reading screenings starting later this month through mid-November. Families wishing to speak to the board on future agenda topics can submit a written delegation request online or in person to Trustee Services.
policyChanges: Trustees are scheduled to consider final approval for Policy #610.0, Reporting Children and Youth in Need of Protection. Additionally, Policy #237.0 on appointing community members to board committees has been moved forward for public review.

title: YRDSB committee scheduled to review speech therapy and special education reports
executiveSummary: A presentation on YRDSB speech-language pathology supports was scheduled for the advisory committee.
Members were set to vote on approving the 2025-2026 Special Education Advisory Committee annual report.
The agenda included a showcase on summer programs for students with developmental disabilities and complex needs.
studentParentImpact: A presentation on speech-language pathology supports was listed on the agenda for York Region District School Board families. The committee was also set to review summer learning programs designed for students with developmental disabilities and multiple special needs. In addition, trustees and committee members were scheduled to vote on approving their annual report detailing special education accomplishments from the previous school year. While this meeting was informational, families can track how YRDSB delivers speech services, specialized summer programming, and ongoing special education supports across York Region schools.
policyChanges: The agenda included routine updates on policies and procedures open for public comment, but no specific policy revisions were scheduled for a vote.

committeeName: Governance and Board Organization Committee Meeting - Public Session
title: YRDSB Agenda: Public Delegation on Bayview Secondary Music Funding
executiveSummary: A public delegation request on funding for Bayview Secondary School's music department was on the YRDSB agenda.
Trustees were set to vote on forming a joint election compliance audit committee with the Catholic board for 2026.
An update report on provincial school board association elections was also on the meeting agenda.
studentParentImpact: The York Region District School Board agenda included a delegate request regarding music department funding at Bayview Secondary School. Community members sought to present concerns about how education funding changes impact music classes, enrolment, and International Baccalaureate students. Trustees were scheduled to decide whether to refer this public presentation to a future committee meeting. The agenda also outlined plans for a joint election audit committee with the Catholic board to review campaign finances for the 2026 school trustee elections. The agenda did not include details on how additional community members could sign up to speak at this specific meeting.
policyChanges: No specific board policies or procedures were scheduled for creation, revision, or rescinding on this agenda.

title: YRDSB agenda set vote on 2026-2027 budget and severe weather policy
executiveSummary: The York Region District School Board scheduled a vote on its 2026-2027 operating budget.
Trustees were set to consider final approval for updated severe weather and communications policies.
The agenda included recommended boundary changes for schools in Richmond Hill, King, and Vaughan.
studentParentImpact: The scheduled vote on the York Region District School Board 2026-2027 operating budget affects funding across all local public schools. Revised severe weather procedures officially split student transportation into two service areas: Georgina and the South Service Area. This means bus cancellations due to extreme weather can happen in one area without affecting the other. The agenda also included school boundary updates creating a new boundary for Dr. Bette Stephenson Secondary School starting in 2027, alongside elementary boundary adjustments for Dr. Roberta Bondar and Forest Run public schools for September 2026.
policyChanges: Policy #105.0 Communications and Policy #152.0 Severe Weather were scheduled for final approval. Staff were also directed to draft revisions for the Operational By-Law and board policies to align with the provincial Putting Student Achievement First Act, 2026.

title: YRDSB scheduled review of updated child protection policy
executiveSummary: Trustees at YRDSB were scheduled to review an updated child protection policy expanding definitions of abuse.
A proposal was on the agenda to open public feedback on how community members join YRDSB committees.
Staff were set to present the upcoming draft schedule for future board policy reviews.
studentParentImpact: An updated YRDSB child protection policy was scheduled for review, expanding safety rules to cover intimate partner violence and sex trafficking. These changes guide how school staff and volunteers report protection concerns for students under 18 years old. Trustees were also set to consider sending a policy on appointing community members to board committees out for six school months of public feedback. Parents and guardians can share feedback on board policies through their school council or by submitting comments to the YRDSB policy officer.
policyChanges: YRDSB Policy #610.0 on reporting children in need of protection was up for second review, and Policy #237.0 on appointing community members to board committees was scheduled for first review.

Families across York Region can review equity initiatives to understand how board staff plan to support diverse student groups and allocate school resources. policyChanges: Policy updates were listed on the agenda for committee review, but no specific policies were named for creation, revision, or repeal.

title: YRDSB set to vote on balanced $1.7B budget amid declining enrolment
executiveSummary: Trustees were set to vote on a balanced $1.7 billion operating budget for the 2026-2027 school year.
The proposed YRDSB budget addresses funding drops driven by declining student enrolment and fewer international students.
An update was also on the agenda for new school construction and classroom additions across York Region.
studentParentImpact: The York Region District School Board draft budget plans for an estimated drop of over 6,600 students for the 2026-2027 school year, leading to a $54 million decrease in overall operating revenue. To maintain balance, the board planned staffing adjustments alongside targeted investments. Proposed spending includes $2 million more for special education equipment, $3.6 million for consistent curriculum resources, and $1.6 million for elementary classroom supplies. The draft budget also maintains funding for primary literacy teachers and math facilitators. Capital updates scheduled for review showed funded school additions in Markham and Aurora alongside new school builds across York Region.
policyChanges: No policy or procedure changes were scheduled for creation, revision, or rescinding on this agenda.

committeeName: Governance and Board Organization Committee Meeting - Public Session
title: YRDSB Agenda Examines PA Day Topics, Exam Rules, and Math Textbook Spending
executiveSummary: The York Region District School Board agenda scheduled a decision on a parent request to reallocate Chromebook funds toward math textbooks.
Trustees were set to review provincial updates detailing mandatory professional activity day topics and new secondary school exam requirements.
The agenda included a recommendation to approve committee meeting dates for the 2027 calendar year.
studentParentImpact: Ontario Ministry of Education directives on the York Region District School Board agenda outline key changes for high school students, including mandatory final written exams and grades tied to attendance and participation. Families will also see four required teacher training topics for the 2026-27 school year, covering artificial intelligence, special education, school safety, and updated curriculum. Additionally, trustees were scheduled to address a parent delegation proposing to shift board funding from student Chromebooks to physical math textbooks. The agenda did not outline a public consultation process or specific instructions for parents to participate in these governance items.
policyChanges: The agenda noted upcoming revisions to the board's operational by-laws and policies to comply with Bill 101, the Putting Student Achievement First Act. No local board policy was up for final vote or repeal during this committee meeting.
